mainTopic: Signs of a תלמיד חכם, and stories of רבי בנאה's wisdom, from מערת המכפלה to becoming a judge
overview: The amud opens by finishing a comparison between the table of a תלמיד חכם and that of an עם הארץ. A second comparison follows, about what each keeps under his bed. Then come stories about רבי בנאה, who marked burial caves. At מערת המכפלה he meets אליעזר, enters אברהם's cave, and is then told by a בת קול not to look at אדם הראשון. He sees only אדם's shining heels, which leads to two chains of beauty: one rising to the שכינה, and one tracing Sages back to אדם הראשון. Next, a dead Sage, רב טובי בר מתנה, grabs a man who was digging up graves. Two more stories show רבי בנאה solving puzzling wills, and the second leads to his arrest. His wife's riddle about a water skin gets him freed and made a judge. At the end he sees a rule on the court gate and begins to challenge it, and his argument continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The table of an ignorant person looks like a bonfire
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes the comparison: the table of an עם הארץ looks like a bonfire with pots all around it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The table of an עם הארץ is like a bonfire, with pots surrounding it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a sentence that started before this section. It describes how an עם הארץ sets his table.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The food sits in the middle like a fire, and plates surround it the way pots surround a bonfire. The table is crowded and messy. This stands in contrast to the neat table of a תלמיד חכם described just before.

keyTerms.meaning: an ignorant person, someone not learned in Torah

phrases.english: to a bonfire, with pots surrounding it.
phrases.notes: This finishes the sentence just before it: an עם הארץ's table is like a bonfire.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the table comparison that began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An עם הארץ's table is cluttered, with food in the center and dishes all around it.

steps.title: What should be under the bed of a Torah scholar
steps.stepSummary: The bed of a תלמיד חכם should have nothing under it except sandals in summer or shoes in winter. The bed of an עם הארץ is like a jumbled storehouse.
steps.simpleTranslation: How should the bed of תלמידי חכמים look? Nothing should be under it except sandals in the summer and shoes in the rainy season. The bed of an עם הארץ looks like a cluttered storehouse.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second comparison in the same style as the table one. This time it is about the space under a bed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A תלמיד חכם keeps only the footwear he needs for that season under his bed, so it stays neat. An עם הארץ piles all kinds of things under his bed. The line asks 'כיצד' and answers it right away, so it works as one teaching statement, not a real back-and-forth.
steps.whatToRemember: A תלמיד חכם's neatness shows even in his table and under his bed. The עם הארץ's messiness is shown in both places too.

phrases.english: The bed of Torah scholars – how should it be?

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל שֶׁאֵין תַּחְתֶּיהָ אֶלָּא סַנְדָּלִין בִּימוֹת הַחַמָּה,
phrases.english: As long as there is nothing under it except sandals in the summer,
and shoes in the rainy season.

phrases.aramaic: וְשֶׁל עַם הָאָרֶץ – דּוֹמָה לְאוֹצָר בָּלוּס.
phrases.english: And the bed of an ignorant person is like a cluttered storehouse.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second comparison in the same pattern as the table comparison.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Under a תלמיד חכם's bed there is only seasonal footwear. Under an עם הארץ's bed everything is piled up.

steps.title: רבי בנאה reaches the cave of אברהם
steps.stepSummary: A new story begins. רבי בנאה was marking caves, and at the cave of אברהם he found אליעזר standing at the entrance.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי בנאה was marking caves. When he reached the cave of אברהם, he found אליעזר, the servant of אברהם, standing in front of the entrance.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new story about רבי בנאה. This line sets the scene for the conversation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The topic moves from personal neatness to an אגדה about the Patriarchs' burial place. רבי בנאה arrives at the cave, and אליעזר is standing guard at the door. That sets up the conversation in the next steps.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי בְּנָאָה הֲוָה קָא מְצַיֵּין מְעָרָתָא.
phrases.english: Rabbi Bena'a was marking caves.
phrases.notes: These are burial caves. Marking them lets people know where graves are.

phrases.english: When he reached the cave of Abraham,
he found Eliezer, the servant of Abraham,
standing in front of the entrance.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי בְּנָאָה הֲוָה קָא מְצַיֵּין מְעָרָתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from the comparisons to a new story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי בנאה, while marking caves, meets אליעזר at the entrance to the cave of אברהם.

steps.title: רבי בנאה asks what אברהם is doing
steps.stepSummary: רבי בנאה asks אליעזר what אברהם is doing right now.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: What is אברהם doing?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי בנאה asks a simple question before going in. He wants to know what is happening inside the cave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He does not just walk in. First he checks what אברהם is busy with, which shows respect. The answer will decide whether it is proper for him to enter.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מַאי קָא עָבֵיד אַבְרָהָם?
phrases.english: He said to him: What is Abraham doing?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי בנאה speaks to אליעזר, whom he just met.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What אברהם is doing at this moment.

steps.title: אליעזר says אברהם is resting with שרה
steps.stepSummary: אליעזר answers that אברהם is lying in שרה's arms and she is examining his head.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: He is lying in the arms of שרה, and she is looking through his head.
steps.whatsHappening: אליעזר answers the question. He describes a private, tender moment between אברהם and שרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The picture is personal and close. This creates a concern: is it proper for a visitor to walk in now? The next step deals with that.

phrases.english: He said to him: He is lying in the arms of Sarah,
and she is examining his head.
phrases.notes: She is looking through his hair, the way one would care for someone close.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי בנאה's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אברהם is lying in שרה's arms while she examines his head.

steps.title: רבי בנאה asks אליעזר to announce him first
steps.stepSummary: רבי בנאה asks אליעזר to tell אברהם that he is standing at the entrance.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Go tell him that בנאה is standing at the entrance.
steps.whatsHappening: Because of the private scene, רבי בנאה asks to be announced first. He wants to give אברהם a chance to get ready for a visitor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a request, but it carries a hidden concern about modesty. רבי בנאה thinks it may not be proper to walk in on them as they are. אליעזר will respond to that concern next.

phrases.english: He said to him: Go tell him:
Bena'a is standing at the entrance.

steps.triggerLanguage: זִיל אֵימָא לֵיהּ: בְּנָאָה קָאֵי אַבָּבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reacts to the private scene described in step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether אברהם should first be told so he can get ready before a visitor enters.

steps.title: No יצר הרע there, so רבי בנאה goes in
steps.stepSummary: אליעזר says רבי בנאה may come in, since there is no evil inclination in that world. רבי בנאה goes in, examines the cave, and leaves.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: Let him come in. It is well known that there is no יצר in this world. He went in, examined the cave, and came out.
steps.whatsHappening: אליעזר answers the modesty concern and tells רבי בנאה he may enter. Then the story ends with רבי בנאה doing his job and leaving.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no יצר הרע in the world where אברהם and שרה are now. So seeing them close together is not improper, and no warning is needed. רבי בנאה goes in only to examine the cave, which was his purpose, and then he leaves.
steps.whatToRemember: אליעזר's answer: in that world there is no יצר הרע. So the usual worry about modesty does not apply, and רבי בנאה could enter, examine the cave, and leave.
steps.confusionAlert: 'בהאי עלמא' here does not mean our world. It means the world where אברהם and שרה are now, the world after this life.

phrases.english: He said to him: Let him enter –

phrases.aramaic: מִידָּע יְדִיעַ דְּיֵצֶר בְּהַאי עָלְמָא לֵיכָּא.
phrases.english: it is well known that there is no evil inclination in this world.
He entered, examined, and went out.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִידָּע יְדִיעַ דְּיֵצֶר בְּהַאי עָלְמָא לֵיכָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the modesty concern raised in step 6 and closes this part of the story.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: There is no need to announce him, because there is no יצר הרע in that world. רבי בנאה enters, examines the cave, and leaves.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Since there is no יצר הרע in the world after this life, entering was not improper.

steps.title: A Heavenly voice forbids looking at אדם הראשון
steps.stepSummary: When רבי בנאה reaches the cave of אדם הראשון, a בת קול tells him he may look at אברהם but not at אדם.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he reached the cave of אדם הראשון, a Heavenly voice came out and said: "You looked at the likeness of My image. Do not look at My image itself."
steps.whatsHappening: The story keeps going. רבי בנאה moves deeper into the cave, toward אדם הראשון, and a בת קול stops him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two levels are set up here. אברהם is only a 'likeness' of God's image, so looking at him was allowed. אדם was made directly in God's image, so looking at him is not allowed.

phrases.english: When he reached the cave of Adam the first man,
a Heavenly voice came out and said:
"You have gazed at the likeness of My image,
phrases.notes: This means אברהם, who looked like אדם.

phrases.english: at My image itself do not gaze."
phrases.notes: This means אדם, who was made in God's image (בראשית 1:27).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story after רבי בנאה left אברהם's cave.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Looking at אברהם was allowed, but looking at אדם הראשון is not.

steps.title: רבי בנאה protests that he must mark the cave
steps.stepSummary: רבי בנאה objects: he needs to look, because his job is to measure and mark the cave.
steps.simpleTranslation: "But I need to mark the cave!"
steps.whatsHappening: רבי בנאה pushes back against the בת קול. If he can't look inside, how can he do his job of marking the cave?
steps.deeperAnalysis: His job of marking the caves (from step 3) seems to clash with the command not to look. This sets up the voice's answer.

keyTerms.meaning: To mark (so people know where the graves are)

phrases.english: "But I need to mark the cave!"
phrases.notes: רבי בנאה is the one speaking, even though the גמרא doesn't say his name.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the command given in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The בת קול's command not to look at אדם's cave
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Marking the cave requires seeing and measuring it, so the command seems to block a necessary task.

steps.title: The inner cave has the same size as the outer cave
steps.stepSummary: The voice answers that the inner cave has the same measurements as the outer one, so there is no need to look.
steps.simpleTranslation: "The measure of the inner cave is the same as the measure of the outer cave."
steps.whatsHappening: The בת קול solves רבי בנאה's problem. He already measured אברהם's cave, so he can use those numbers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both needs are met: רבי בנאה can mark the cave, and he still doesn't look at אדם. The outer cave is אברהם's, and the inner one is אדם's.

phrases.english: "Like the measurement of the outer one,
so is the measurement of the inner one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the protest in step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Provides another way to get the needed information
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Marking the cave would require looking inside.
steps.terutzMaskana: The size is the same as the outer cave, so there is no need to look.

steps.title: The same answer for the view that the rooms are stacked
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rewords the voice's answer for the opinion that the cave had two rooms, one above the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the one who says the cave had two rooms, one on top of the other, the voice said: "The lower one is the same size as the upper one."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adjusts the wording of the answer to fit another opinion about how the cave was built.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is the same. Only the layout changes: 'outer and inner' becomes 'upper and lower.'

keyTerms.meaning: And according to the one who says

phrases.aramaic: וּלְמַאן דְּאָמַר שְׁנֵי בָתִּים זוֹ לְמַעְלָה מִזּוֹ –
phrases.english: And according to the one who says it was two rooms, one above the other —
like the measurement of the upper one, so is the measurement of the lower one."

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְמַאן דְּאָמַר שְׁנֵי בָתִּים זוֹ לְמַעְלָה מִזּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the step 10 answer in the form that fits a different view of the cave's layout.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Same answer, reworded for another opinion
steps.terutzMaskana: Either way, the hidden room matches the one already measured.

steps.title: אדם's heels shone like two suns
steps.stepSummary: רבי בנאה reports that he saw אדם הראשון's heels, and they shone like two suns.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי בנאה said: I looked at his two heels, and they looked like two suns.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי בנאה describes the little he did see of אדם הראשון: just his heels.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even the lowest part of אדם's body shone like the sun. This leads into the next lines about beauty.

phrases.english: Rabbi Bena'a said:
I gazed at his two heels,
and they look like two orbs of the sun.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי בְּנָאָה נִסְתַּכַּלְתִּי בִּשְׁנֵי עֲקֵיבָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tells what רבי בנאה actually saw of אדם.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אדם הראשון's heels shone like two suns.

steps.title: A chain of beauty from שרה up to the שכינה
steps.stepSummary: Each level looks like a monkey next to a person when compared to the level above it: everyone to שרה, שרה to חוה, חוה to אדם, and אדם to the שכינה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Everyone next to שרה is like a monkey next to a person. שרה next to חוה is like a monkey next to a person. חוה next to אדם is like a monkey next to a person. אדם next to the שכינה is like a monkey next to a person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a ladder of beauty to show how much greater each level is than the one below it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same comparison repeats at every rung. Even אדם, whose heels shone like suns, is like a monkey compared to the שכינה.

phrases.aramaic: הַכֹּל בִּפְנֵי שָׂרָה – כְּקוֹף בִּפְנֵי אָדָם.
phrases.english: Everyone compared to Sarah is like a monkey compared to a person.

phrases.aramaic: שָׂרָה בִּפְנֵי חַוָּה – כְּקוֹף בִּפְנֵי אָדָם.
phrases.english: Sarah compared to Eve is like a monkey compared to a person.

phrases.aramaic: חַוָּה בִּפְנֵי אָדָם – כְּקוֹף בִּפְנֵי אָדָם.
phrases.english: Eve compared to Adam is like a monkey compared to a person.
phrases.notes: The first אדם is Adam himself. The second just means 'a person.'

phrases.aramaic: אָדָם בִּפְנֵי שְׁכִינָה – כְּקוֹף בִּפְנֵי אָדָם.
phrases.english: Adam compared to the Divine Presence is like a monkey compared to a person.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַכֹּל בִּפְנֵי שָׂרָה כְּקוֹף בִּפְנֵי אָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the description of אדם's beauty.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each level of beauty is far beyond the one below it, all the way up to the שכינה.

steps.title: A chain of beauty from רב כהנא back to אדם הראשון
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא's beauty reflects רב's, רב's reflects רבי אבהו's, his reflects יעקב אבינו's, and יעקב's reflects אדם הראשון's.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא's beauty is a reflection of רב's beauty. רב's beauty is a reflection of רבי אבהו's. רבי אבהו's is a reflection of יעקב אבינו's. יעקב אבינו's is a reflection of אדם הראשון's.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second beauty chain, this time tracing famous Sages back to אדם הראשון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here each person carries a trace of the beauty of the one above. The chain ends again at אדם הראשון, tying it back to the story.

phrases.aramaic: שׁוּפְרֵיהּ דְּרַב כָּהֲנָא מֵעֵין שׁוּפְרֵיהּ דְּרַב,
phrases.english: The beauty of Rav Kahana is a reflection of the beauty of Rav,

phrases.aramaic: שׁוּפְרֵיהּ דְּרַב מֵעֵין שׁוּפְרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אֲבָהוּ,
phrases.english: the beauty of Rav is a reflection of the beauty of Rabbi Abbahu,

phrases.aramaic: שׁוּפְרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אֲבָהוּ מֵעֵין שׁוּפְרֵיהּ דְּיַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ,
phrases.english: the beauty of Rabbi Abbahu is a reflection of the beauty of Jacob our forefather,

phrases.aramaic: שׁוּפְרֵיהּ דְּיַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ מֵעֵין שׁוּפְרֵיהּ דְּאָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן.
phrases.english: the beauty of Jacob our forefather is a reflection of the beauty of Adam the first man.

steps.triggerLanguage: שׁוּפְרֵיהּ דְּרַב כָּהֲנָא מֵעֵין שׁוּפְרֵיהּ דְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second beauty chain, parallel to step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The beauty of great people reflects, step by step, the beauty of אדם הראשון.
steps.whatToRemember: Both chains point back to אדם הראשון as the high point of human beauty, and the first chain goes even higher, to the שכינה.

steps.title: A grave-digger is grabbed by the beard
steps.stepSummary: An אמגושא who dug up graves was grabbed by the beard by the dead רב טובי בר מתנה, and אביי asked רב טובי to let him go.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was an אמגושא who used to dig up the dead. When he reached the cave of רב טובי בר מתנה, רב טובי grabbed him by his beard. אביי came and said to him: Please, let him go.
steps.whatsHappening: A new story about burial caves begins. A dead Sage grabs a man who was disturbing graves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This story shows that the righteous dead still react when their graves are disturbed. אביי steps in and asks for mercy, and the story continues in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: He grabbed him by his beard

phrases.english: There was a certain magus who used to dig up the dead.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי מְטָא אַמְּעָרְתָּא דְּרַב טוֹבִי בַּר מַתְנָה,
phrases.english: When he reached the burial cave of Rav Tovi bar Mattana,
he grabbed him by his beard.
phrases.notes: רב טובי, the dead Sage, is the one grabbing the magus.

phrases.english: Abaye came and said to him:
I beg of you, let him go.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new story on the shared theme of burial caves.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב טובי, though dead, grabbed the grave-digger, and let him go when אביי asked.

steps.title: The second time, his beard has to be cut off
steps.stepSummary: The next year the אמגושא came back and was grabbed again, and this time רב טובי would not let go until אביי cut off the man's beard.
steps.simpleTranslation: The next year he came back, and רב טובי grabbed him by his beard. אביי came, but רב טובי did not let go until אביי brought scissors and cut off his beard.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends. The man came back to do it again, so this time a request was not enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first time, אביי's request freed him. Because he came back, רב טובי refused, and the only way to free him was to cut off his beard.

phrases.english: The next year he came again,
and he grabbed him by his beard.
Abaye came,
but he did not let him go
until he brought scissors and cut off his beard.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the story begun in step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the man came back, רב טובי held on until his beard was cut off.
steps.whatToRemember: The first time a request was enough. When the man came back to do it again, he was held until his beard was cut off.

steps.title: A father's confusing will about three barrels
steps.stepSummary: A dying man leaves a barrel of earth, a barrel of bones and a barrel of wool wads to his three sons. The sons do not understand and go to רבי בנאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A man said: a barrel of earth to one son, a barrel of bones to another, a barrel of wool wads to another. They didn't know what he meant, so they came to רבי בנאה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new story about רבי בנאה by presenting a puzzle: a will nobody understands. This step sets up the question that רבי בנאה will answer next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The father's words sound strange because nobody inherits barrels of dirt or bones. The sons cannot divide the property until someone explains the hidden meaning, so they bring it to a wise person.

phrases.english: There was a certain man who said to them:
phrases.notes: He means his family, right before he died.

phrases.english: A barrel of earth to one of my sons,
a barrel of bones to one of my sons,
a barrel of wool wads to one of my sons.

phrases.aramaic: לָא הֲווֹ יָדְעִי מַאי קָאָמַר לְהוּ.
phrases.english: They did not know what he was saying to them.
They came before Rabbi Bena'a.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the stories about רב טובי בר מתנה, the גמרא returns to stories about רבי בנאה, who was mentioned in step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A will was given in puzzling language, and the heirs needed it explained.

steps.title: רבי בנאה decodes the three barrels
steps.stepSummary: רבי בנאה asks whether they inherited land, animals and quilts. They say yes, and he explains that this is what the father meant.
steps.simpleTranslation: He asked: Do you have land? Yes. Animals? Yes. Quilts? Yes. Then that is what he meant.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי בנאה solves the riddle by asking what kinds of property the father left. Each barrel stands for one type of property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earth stands for land, bones stand for animals, and wool stands for quilts and bedding. By checking that the estate really had all three, רבי בנאה confirms his reading, and each son gets one category.

phrases.english: He said to them: Do you have land?
They said to him: Yes.
Do you have animals? Yes.
Do you have quilts? Yes.
If so, this is what he was telling you.
phrases.notes: Earth means land, bones mean animals, and wool means the quilts. Each son gets one of these.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the puzzle raised in step 17.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What did the father mean by the three barrels?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Earth means land, bones mean animals, and wool means quilts. Each son gets one type of property.

steps.title: A man learns only one son is his
steps.stepSummary: A man overhears his wife admit to their daughter that only one of her ten sons is his. When he is dying, he leaves all his property to one son.
steps.simpleTranslation: A man heard his wife tell their daughter: Why aren't you discreet when you sin? I have ten sons and only one is from your father. When he was dying he said: All my property to one son.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a second story about a puzzling will. This step sets up the problem: the father did not say which son he meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The father found out that only one son was really his, so he left everything to that son. He did not name him, so nobody knows who gets the property.

keyTerms.meaning: you act discreetly, hide what you do

phrases.english: There was a certain man who heard his wife
saying to her daughter:
Why are you not discreet when you sin?

phrases.aramaic: הָךְ אִיתְּתָא, עֲשָׂרָה בְּנֵי אִית לַהּ,
phrases.english: That woman has ten sons,
phrases.notes: "That woman" is her polite way of saying "I."

phrases.english: and I have only one from your father.
When he was dying, he said to them:
All my property to one son.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second unclear-will story, parallel to the barrels story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A father left everything to his one true son without saying who he was.

steps.title: The grave test reveals the true son
steps.stepSummary: The sons ask רבי בנאה. He tells them to strike their father's grave. All go except one, and רבי בנאה gives that son all the property.
steps.simpleTranslation: They didn't know which son. רבי בנאה said: Go hit your father's grave until he gets up and tells you. They all went except the real son. He said: All the property goes to this one.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי בנאה uses a clever test to find the true son. The son who refuses to disrespect his father's grave shows that he is the real son.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Striking a father's grave is a shameful act, and only a real son would refuse to do it to his own father. רבי בנאה reads the sons' behavior as the evidence, not witnesses or documents.

phrases.english: They did not know to which of them.
They came before Rabbi Bena'a.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ: זִילוּ חֲבוּטוּ קִבְרָא דַּאֲבוּכוֹן,
phrases.english: He said to them: Go strike your father's grave,
until he rises and reveals to you
to which of you he left it.
They all went.
The one who was really his son did not go.
He said to them: All the property belongs to this one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Solves the problem set up in step 19.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which son did the father mean?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The son who would not strike his father's grave is the true son and inherits everything.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי בנאה did not really expect the father to rise from the grave. The instruction was a test to see which son would refuse to shame his father.

steps.title: The brothers slander רבי בנאה to the king
steps.stepSummary: The angry brothers tell the king that a Jew is taking people's money without witnesses or evidence, and רבי בנאה is arrested.
steps.simpleTranslation: They went and slandered him at the king's palace, saying: There is a Jew who takes money from people without witnesses or anything. They brought him and jailed him.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues: the brothers who lost the inheritance take revenge by informing on רבי בנאה, and he is jailed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their complaint attacks his method. He ruled from the sons' behavior and had no עדים or other proof, so to the king it looked like he was taking money for no reason.

keyTerms.meaning: the king's house, the royal court

phrases.english: They went and slandered him in the king's house.
phrases.notes: "They" are the brothers who got nothing.

phrases.english: They said: There is a man among the Jews
who takes money away from people
without witnesses and without anything.
They brought him and imprisoned him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The result of רבי בנאה's ruling in step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי בנאה is jailed on the charge that he takes money without witnesses or evidence.

steps.title: רבי בנאה's wife presents a riddle
steps.stepSummary: רבי בנאה's wife goes to the authorities with a strange complaint about a servant whose head was cut off, who was skinned and eaten, and who is now used to carry water without payment to her.
steps.simpleTranslation: His wife went and said: I had a servant. They cut off his head, skinned him, ate his meat, and now they fill him with water and give their friends drinks from him, and they don't pay me his value or his rent.
steps.whatsHappening: His wife enters the story with a puzzling complaint. This step sets up a test of whether the officials can understand her riddle, which the גמרא continues with next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her words cannot be literal, because no one fills a dead servant with water. Like the father's will in step 17, it is a riddle with a hidden meaning that needs to be decoded.

phrases.english: His wife went and said to them:
phrases.notes: This is רבי בנאה's wife speaking to the king's men.

phrases.english: I had one servant.
They cut off his head,
skinned him and ate his flesh,
and they fill him with water
phrases.notes: This can't be literal. It's a riddle, and רבי בנאה explains it in step 24.

phrases.english: and give their friends to drink from him,

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא קָא יָהֲבִי לִי דְּמֵי וְלָא אַגְרֵיהּ.
phrases.english: and they do not give me his value or his rent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the imprisonment story: his wife acts to help free him.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The wife puts a riddle-style complaint before the authorities. Its meaning is revealed later.

steps.title: The authorities cannot understand the riddle
steps.stepSummary: The officials do not understand the wife's strange complaint and decide to call the wise man of the Jews to explain it.
steps.simpleTranslation: They did not know what she was talking about. They said: Let us bring the wise man of the Jews and let him explain it.
steps.whatsHappening: The officials are puzzled by the wife's riddle and decide to bring in a wise Jew to explain it. This sets up the next step, where the wise man is called.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wife's complaint about a servant who was beheaded, skinned, eaten, and now carries water made no sense on its plain meaning. Because the officials are stuck, they need an expert. The expert they turn to is the very man they had arrested, רבי בנאה.

keyTerms.meaning: The wise man of the Jews

phrases.aramaic: לָא יָדְעִי מַאי קָא אָמְרָה לְהוּ.
phrases.english: They did not know what she was saying to them.
They said: Let us bring the wise man of the Jews, and let him say what she meant.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא יָדְעִי מַאי קָא אָמְרָה לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reacts to the wife's riddle from step 22 by asking for an explanation.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What did the wife mean by her strange complaint about the servant?

steps.title: רבי בנאה solves the riddle: a water skin
steps.stepSummary: רבי בנאה is called in and explains that the wife was talking about a water skin.
steps.simpleTranslation: They called רבי בנאה. He said to them: She was telling you about a water skin.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי בנאה is brought in and solves the riddle: the 'servant' was really a goat whose skin became a water skin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The goat was slaughtered (its 'head cut off'), skinned and eaten, and its skin was made into a water skin that 'carries water'. The wife was complaining that people were using her water skin without paying her. Her riddle got her husband out of prison and in front of the officials, where his wisdom could be seen.

keyTerms.meaning: A water skin (a container made from an animal's hide)

phrases.english: They called Rabbi Bena'a,
he said to them: She spoke to you of a water skin.
phrases.notes: The 'servant' was her goat. It was slaughtered and eaten, and its skin was made into a bag for carrying water.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 23 by explaining the riddle.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The wife was talking about a water skin made from her slaughtered goat.

steps.title: רבי בנאה is made a judge
steps.stepSummary: Impressed by his wisdom, the officials decide that רבי בנאה should sit at the gate and judge cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: Since he is so wise, let him sit at the gate and judge.
steps.whatsHappening: The officials are so impressed that, instead of punishing רבי בנאה, they appoint him a judge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story turns around completely. רבי בנאה was arrested for ruling without witnesses, and now he is officially made a דיין. His wisdom, shown through the riddle, proves that his earlier rulings were not random.

phrases.english: They said: Since he is so wise,
let him sit at the gate and render judgment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the result of the solved riddle: רבי בנאה is freed and appointed a judge.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Instead of being punished, רבי בנאה is made a judge because of his wisdom.
steps.whatToRemember: The man arrested for 'judging without evidence' ends up appointed as an official judge.

steps.title: The inscription on the gate
steps.stepSummary: רבי בנאה sees a rule written on the gate: a judge who is summoned to court is no longer considered a judge.
steps.simpleTranslation: He saw that it was written on the gate: Any judge who is called to court is not called a judge.
steps.whatsHappening: The story presents a rule written on the court's gate. This sets up רבי בנאה's challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The inscription teaches that a דיין must be above reproach. If he himself is ever summoned to court, he loses his standing as a judge. רבי בנאה is about to show that this rule, taken as written, makes no sense.

phrases.english: He saw that it was written upon the gate:
Any judge who is summoned to judgment
is not considered a judge.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that רבי בנאה sits at the gate, he notices the rule written there.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A judge who is summoned to court loses his status as a judge.

steps.title: רבי בנאה begins to challenge the inscription
steps.stepSummary: רבי בנאה starts to argue that the gate's rule cannot be right, beginning with the case of a stranger who comes from elsewhere.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: If so, then if a person comes from elsewhere...
steps.whatsHappening: רבי בנאה begins to attack the rule on the gate with 'אלא מעתה'. His argument continues past the end of this section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'אלא מעתה' signals that he is about to show an absurd result of the rule. He is starting to describe a stranger who comes from elsewhere. That stranger could summon a judge to court, and under the inscription the judge would then lose his position.

keyTerms.meaning: If that is so (introduces an absurd result)
From elsewhere, from the outside world

steps.confusionAlert: The thought is not finished here. The rest of רבי בנאה's challenge comes right after this section.

phrases.english: He said to them: If that is so,
a person comes from elsewhere

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the inscription quoted in step 26.
steps.kashyaTarget: The inscription that a judge summoned to court is no longer a judge.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Taken as written, the rule would lead to an absurd result, starting with an outsider who comes from elsewhere. The full argument continues in the next part of the text.
